written_before: any candidate was evaluated against these gates (the first evaluation is the weekly pipeline's bootstrap run recorded in registry/history.jsonl)
scope: operational champion of the NCAAM pregame forecast (basketball/ncaam_forecast). Does NOT change the research registry tier: SIM/forecast research status stays EXPERIMENTAL until the separate research criteria in research/registration.json pass.

evaluation.games: D1-v-D1 games scored walk-forward (causal ratings; calibration fitted weekly on earlier games only)
evaluation.window: every complete season from 2020 to the last complete season, plus the season in progress to date (rolling origin: each game predicted only from what was available 30 minutes before tip)
evaluation.excluded: NCAA tournament games of the final tournament holdout seasons 2024, 2025, 2026 (never used to choose or promote anything)
evaluation.pairing: champion and challenger scored on the SAME games; differences challenger minus champion; 95% intervals by bootstrap clustered on game day (1,000 resamples)

G1_min_sample.rule: at least 15000 shared scored games and at least 3 seasons in the window
G1_min_sample.why: below about 15,000 games the 95% interval of a log-loss difference between two good models is wider than the 0.0002 gain required (measured half-width ~0.00025 at 37,600 games)

G2_log_loss.rule: mean difference <= -0.0002 AND the 95% interval's upper bound < 0
G2_log_loss.why: 0.0002 is the noise floor the existing basketball loop already uses (basketball/loop.js MIN_GAIN.logloss); requiring the interval below zero rejects gains the data cannot distinguish from chance

G3_brier.why: a log-loss gain bought with worse Brier would mean the gain sits in extreme probabilities only

G4_margin_crps.why: the margin distribution is what spreads, totals and the simulator read; 0.002 is the research engine's challenger margin (3% of the spread between configurations)

G5_calibration.rule: challenger in the window: |calibration-in-the-large| <= 0.015, logistic recalibration slope within [0.90, 1.10], 80% margin and total interval coverage within [0.77, 0.83], |forecast - observed overtime rate| <= 0.01
G5_calibration.why: measured on the current champion candidate's development window: citl 0.005-0.011, slope 1.04-1.07, coverage 0.80; the bounds leave room for that and refuse a visibly miscalibrated challenger

G6_cohorts.rule: no gated cohort is worse by more than 0.002 log loss with its 95% interval entirely above 0; cohorts with fewer than 300 shared games are reported, not gated
G6_cohorts.why: an aggregate gain must not hide a real regression where it matters most in March (neutral sites, postseason) or for poorly observed teams

G7_integrity.rule: dataset hashes match the manifest; no row predicted with an input known after its prediction time; the training snapshot hash is recorded; rebuilding the artifact twice gives the same sha256
G7_integrity.why: a model is only as honest as its inputs

G8_operations.rule: the weekly run finishes within 45 minutes; every probability is finite and inside (0, 1)

decisions.PROMOTE: every gate passes: the challenger's artifact becomes champion through the atomic pointer swap (registry.js), the previous champion stays as the rollback target
decisions.RETAIN: any gate G2-G8 fails: the champion is unchanged
decisions.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: G1 fails: nothing is promoted, whatever the point estimates say
decisions.one_per_week: at most one promotion per weekly run (the passing challenger with the largest log-loss gain)
